headline: Kai, Democrats swept Congress, the Dow logged its best day since April 2025, and the AI trade is doing the math on a tougher regulatory map.
subline: Nasdaq futures lag on data-center politics, oil's four-day slide pauses near $89, and a Bank of England hike is expected this morning.
asof: Pre-market · futures and overnight quotes as of ~6:40 AM ET · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Dow's best day since April 2025; futures split
items.sentence: Wednesday's sweep rally carried the Dow up 1,569 points to 53,356.12 and the S&P 500 up 1.58% to 7,688.62, and this morning Dow futures hold green while Nasdaq futures give some of it back, per StockTitan and Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Oil steadies near $89 after an 8% rout
items.sentence: WTI settled 8% lower at $88.12 on Wednesday — a fourth straight decline built on hopes a weakened White House now deals with Iran — and trades near $88.87 this morning, per Yahoo Finance and StockTitan.

items.title: BoE hike expected; claims and productivity today
items.sentence: The Bank of England is expected to raise rates 25 basis points to 4% this morning, its first hike of the cycle, ahead of US jobless claims and third-quarter productivity, with futures still pricing a December Fed hike, per XTB.

items.title: Toyota raises outlook; ConocoPhillips and Airbnb today
items.sentence: Toyota beat with ¥1.13 trillion in operating profit, lifted its full-year forecast to ¥3.90 trillion and expanded its buyback, with ConocoPhillips due this morning and Airbnb after the close, per XTB and Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Bitcoin back above $80,000
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades at $80,255, up 2.4% on the day, recovering an election-night dip that came as traders read a Democratic Congress as slower digital-asset deregulation, per Yahoo Finance and The Standard.

items.title: Democrats take the House and the Senate
items.sentence: Democrats won control of both chambers — CNBC counts at least 54 Senate seats and at least 250 in the House — with Republicans failing to flip a single seat, per CNBC.

items.title: Vance blames the Iran war; Trump concurs
items.sentence: JD Vance said the war with Iran cost Republicans the Congress, Trump called that explanation 'largely true,' and Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek the minority-leader post, per The Standard.

items.title: Schumer: the war 'must end'
items.sentence: Chuck Schumer said the Iran war 'must end' and suggested the new majority could press the point through government funding, while Qatar-mediated talks leave the sides, in Tehran's words, 'still far apart,' per The Standard and XTB.

items.title: Allies begin planning Ukraine's post-war reconstruction
items.sentence: Delegations from the US, Ukraine, Germany, France and Britain met with NATO and the World Bank to discuss rebuilding Ukraine after the war, according to the EU, per The Standard.

items.title: Texas elects a Democratic governor and senator
items.sentence: Gina Hinojosa won the governorship on promises of tougher data-center rules and James Talarico beat Ken Paxton for the Senate, a race in which Elon Musk's record $224 million was not enough, per XTB.

items.title: Data-center stocks pay for the sweep
items.sentence: Hut 8 fell 23% and Ohio voters passed data-center restrictions in at least 14 municipalities, with Goldman estimating 45% of planned US capacity sits in states that could now tighten rules, per AI Weekly and XTB.

items.title: Qualcomm and Arm wobble after earnings
items.sentence: Qualcomm dropped about 7.4% after hours on soft guidance with smartphone-chip revenue down 26% year over year, and Arm slipped as royalty revenue came in light, per XTB.

items.title: Korea's chip trade cracks; Kospi −4.8%
items.sentence: A 4.8% Kospi drop tripped Seoul's five-minute program-trading halt and SK Hynix lost about 9%, leaving the index roughly 40% below its June peak, per XTB.

items.title: Anthropic licenses AP's real-time election data
items.sentence: Anthropic struck a deal for Associated Press real-time election feeds, in what AI Weekly calls its first paid content-licensing agreement with a digital publisher.

items.title: UBS lifts AI capex forecast to $1.4 trillion
items.sentence: UBS now sees $1.4 trillion in AI infrastructure spending even as Citrini Research argues investment growth has peaked and the risk has tilted down, per XTB.
